Nothing built yet. Two jobs in one: first every portal’s ad has to say where the item is with a country and postal code — only Motor does that today, the rest store a typed-in place name or nothing at all — and only then can “nearest to me” sort anything. Roughly half the time is the sweep across the other portals, half is the location service itself: asking permission the moment someone presses Nearest and never before, and the three ways to answer — share where you are, type a postal code, or point at a map.

The engine works on Dev: paste the address of your advert on another site and it comes back as a draft in our own create form — text, price and photos in order, a lock so the same advert can never be imported twice, and a gate so only verified people and registered businesses can import. In review now: the whole-page import — paste a seller's overview page and every advert on it comes back as its own draft, with progress shown and any that could not come over named with the reason. An advert comes across exactly as it stands on the other site: no text is rewritten on its own. Country and postal code always arrive empty and the seller fills them before publishing, so nothing publishes without them. Left: (1) the side-by-side rewrite — on one draft the seller presses a button, sees the original and a suggestion next to each other, and chooses; (2) the copy-protection review queue — until it lands, first to publish holds a URL; (3) the entry on the remaining portals — Real Estate, short-term rent, Marketplace.

Files people upload as evidence in a complaint or with a business application no longer sit at permanent open addresses — uploads are signed, the files are private, and reading one takes a short-lived link that only the people already allowed on that page can mint. The cleanup ran and the proof is posted: the photo store held no open documents anywhere, and the one document store that was publicly readable is now closed and proven closed with a fresh read. Fatsees Equity is a noticeboard where owners of private-company shares advertise
them for sale — legal without a licence only if we never match buyers and sellers,
host deal chat, show live prices, or touch the money.
I'm adding those legal guardrails, removing old features that crossed the line,
and building the allowed ones (contact reveal, wanted ads, history chart, alerts).
In short: Equity must always behave like a noticeboard, never like a stock exchange.
Prod-gated: silent-fallback confirmation and the full acceptance test on prod — waits on Victor's main-branch merge.

Closed — nothing to clean up.

When we removed the share-ownership verification feature on 27 July, we deleted the database records but not the documents users had uploaded with them. Those documents would have been left sitting in our file storage with no owner attached — which GDPR doesn't allow, because nobody could find them to delete them if a user asked.

Checked, and there are none. The file storage account has never held a single uploaded document of any kind, on any part of the site. Nothing was left behind, so there is nothing to delete.

Shipped anyway so it can't happen next time: a reusable cleanup tool, plus a new question on the PR review checklist — if this change deletes a table that points at uploaded files, where do the files get cleaned up?

Still open, on me: the backup snapshot we were supposed to take before deleting those records doesn't look like it was taken. Tracked on its own card.

Lets an admin give a business account a paid plan for free until a chosen date — useful for launch partners and campaigns. Reminders go out 30, 14, 7 and 1 days before it runs out. If nobody pays after that, their ads go quiet rather than being deleted, and come straight back the moment payment arrives.

The one thing that must not go wrong: if a granted business saves a card to buy something small — an ad, some tokens — the system must not read that as "start charging them for the subscription". They were given the period; the date decides, nothing else.

Paid promotion slots, and the free ones that fill in when nobody has paid. Equity is one of those three: paying to promote an investment to ordinary people is exactly what that portal must never do.
